newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-NATAL SWEEP PAST KENYA INTO SEMI-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NATAL SWEEP PAST KENYA INTO SEMI-FINALS.

text.p: and Mashonaland in the semi-finals of the Standard Bank Cup
cricket competition after an emphatic 104-run victory over Kenya
in their quarter-final match at Kingsmead on Wednesday.
The 1996-97 SuperSport Series champions stayed on course for
a possible domestic double after posting a challenging 240 for
six batting first. They then dismissed Kenya for a paltry 136 in
Kenya, who play in the International Cricket Council Trophy
in Malaysia later this month, got off to a useful start with an
opening partnership of 32 between Asif Karim (13) and Kennedy
But the cheap dismissal of their key batsmen -- Otieno,
Steve Tikolo (for two) and captain Maurice Odumbe (eight) -- put
Kenya on the back foot and they lost wickets at regular
intervals as the pressure of chasing 241 told.
All-rounder Thomas Odoyo produced a spanking 21 off 28 balls
towards the end but Natal outclassed their visitors in the field
with Neil Johnson taking 4-19 and off-spinner Pat Symcox 3-22.
Earlier, the home side were boosted by a fourth-wicket
partnership of 145 between opener Doug Watson and all-rounder
Derek Crookes as they made their impressive 240 for six after
Watson, who top-scored with a patient 85, and Crookes, who
was made man of the match for his aggressive 72 from 84 balls
and his display in the field, hit Natal out of early innings
trouble when they had been pegged back to 33 for three in the
Man of the match: Derek Crookes.
